measure: edge length of the container divided by the edge length of the pieces
format: [x, y, z, qw, qx, qy, qz] per canonical piece; scalar-first quaternion; container = s_full times canonical container
method: soft-to-rigid homotopy (inscribed balls hardened into the solid under inward pressure), then SLSQP tightening with per-pair separating planes
title: 32 tetrahedra in an icosahedron
credit: soft-to-rigid method by Yohei Nakajima (2026); generalization to Platonic solids, basin-hopping search and exact certification developed with Claude (Anthropic) under Alejandro Zarzuelo's direction

contribution.method:
Batch of 799 witnesses in 24 problems (`MANIFEST.json` + `records/<record_id>.json` + `SUMMARY.tsv`), each at least 1e-4 (relative) below the current `records/SUMMARY.csv` entry (main at 176e2c2e, checked 2026-10-29). Every record passes `verify_general.py` (VALID) and `certify_general.py` (CERTIFIED) from that commit locally, run on the files extracted from the archive. The changes against the current records: median -1.66 %, largest -13.39 %; 498 records improve by ≥ 1 %, 692 by ≥ 0.1 %.

**Relation to earlier submissions.** #98–#103 (including #101 and #102 from sinkomr) were merged into 176e2c2e on 2026-10-28; every record here is at least 1e-4 (relative) below the value in that archive.

**Against PolyPack.** I also compared with PolyPack's published records (https://github.com/sinkomr/PolyPack, `data/polyhedra/records.json`, fetched 2026-10-29) and kept only records that are at least 1e-4 below both the archive and PolyPack (463 of these records have a PolyPack value; `SUMMARY.tsv` lists both values, `polypack_s`, `change_vs_best`).

**How the records were made.** `found_by`, `credit` and `method` identify where each record starts; `method` or `refinement` gives the steps.

- *Refinements of catalogue records* (238): a contact-preserving descent (sequential linear programming with the contacts as inequalities) started from the catalogue record named in `refinement`. `found_by`, `credit` and `method` are the catalogue record's own, copied verbatim; my part is in `refined_by` and `refinement_credit`. For 199 of them the start was the record for a different n and the first n pieces were kept (`derived_from`). Rigidity analysis and code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23630728
- *Lattice cuts* (476): all pieces in one orientation at the points of a lattice inside the container, orientation and position of the container optimised, then a descent as above.
- *Cell compositions* (85): the container is divided into cells and each cell is filled with a catalogue record

refinement: starting from tetinico_n32 (catalogue at e0fc3211): contact-preserving descent (rigidity analysis: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23630728); centres expanded by 3e-7 and the container sized for a 2e-7 wall gap
